title: SPARK CSEC Physics - Paper 01 Practice Paper 13
subject: Physics
syllabus: CXC 22/G/SYLL 13, for examinations from May and June 2015
instructions: This test consists of 60 items. You will have 1 hour and 15 minutes to answer them.
Each item has four suggested answers lettered A, B, C and D. Choose the best answer.
If you cannot answer an item, move on and return to it later.
Figures are not necessarily drawn to scale.
You may use a silent, non-programmable calculator.

items.stem: Placing a door handle far from the hinge makes the door easier to turn because it gives

options.text: a smaller moment for the same force

misconception.label: A greater distance gives a greater moment, not a smaller one.

options.text: a smaller force for the same moment at the hinge

items.objective_statement: state Newton’s three laws of motion
items.stem: Which statement expresses Newton's third law?

options.text: every action has a larger reaction

misconception.label: The two forces are equal in size, not one larger than the other.

options.text: action and reaction act on the same body and cancel

misconception.label: They act on different bodies, which is exactly why they do not cancel.

options.text: if A exerts a force on B, then B exerts an equal and opposite force on A
the reaction always follows the action after a short delay

misconception.label: The two forces appear and disappear together, with no delay.

steps: Push on a wall and the wall pushes back on the hand with the same size of force.
The two forces act on different bodies, the wall and the hand.
Because they act on different bodies, they cannot cancel one another; each has its own effect.
solution.answer_line: if A exerts a force on B, then B exerts an equal and opposite force on A

items.stem: While ice melts at 0 °C, its temperature remains constant because the energy supplied is

options.text: escaping to the surroundings as fast as it is supplied

misconception.label: It would still warm up between losses; the constant temperature holds even in an insulated container.

options.text: being used to separate the particles of the ice rather than speed them up
too small to raise the temperature

misconception.label: The same supply raises the temperature readily once all the ice has melted.

options.text: being stored as pressure in the water

misconception.label: Water in an open beaker is not under increased pressure.

steps: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the particles.
While the ice melts, the supplied energy does work separating particles from the lattice.

items.objective_statement: distinguish between evaporation and boiling
items.stem: Blowing air across water increases its rate of evaporation because the moving air

options.text: raises the temperature of the water

misconception.label: Moving air cools the water, it does not warm it.

options.text: lowers the atmospheric pressure on the surface

misconception.label: A fan does not change the atmospheric pressure noticeably.

options.text: adds energy to the water molecules

misconception.label: The energy for escape comes from the liquid itself, which is why it cools.

options.text: carries away escaped molecules so fewer return to the liquid

steps: The fastest molecules at the surface escape; some in the vapour above come back.
A fan sweeps the escaped molecules away before they can return.

solution.answer_line: tiny liquid droplets condensed on ions
